title: [Bug]: extract_hidden_states overestimates DeepSeek-V4 KV cache memory
body:
## Your current environment

The failing baseline and patched run used the same image, model, hardware, and
serving configuration. The patched run replaced only the vLLM wheel.

```text
Base image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0-cu129-ubuntu2404
Baseline vLLM: 0.26.0+cu129
Fix validation vLLM: 0.26.1rc1.dev657+g793ca6998.cu129
Fix source commit: 793ca6998adfa5a3ab22d6012dee78044b8ba901
OS: Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS (x86_64)
Python: 3.12.3
PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu129
CUDA runtime: 12.9.86
NVIDIA driver: 580.159.03
GPU: 4 x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3
Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash
Tensor parallelism: TP=4
Hidden-state layers: 40, 41, 42, and the final layer 43
Hidden-state dtype and size: bf16, 4096
KV cache dtype: fp8
Cache block size: 256
Maximum model length: 8192
Prefix caching: enabled
CUDA Graph mode: FULL_DECODE_ONLY
```

## 🐛 Describe the bug

Enabling hidden-state extraction on DeepSeek-V4 causes the KV-cache capacity
calculation to overestimate the required memory and reject engine startup after
the model has loaded successfully.

With TP=4 on four H100 80GB GPUs, the model uses approximately 38.87 GiB per
GPU. The subsequent KV-cache validation incorrectly reports that an 8,192-token
request requires 581.48 GiB of KV-cache memory:

```text
ValueError: To serve at least one request with the model's max seq len (8192),
(581.48 GiB KV cache is needed, which is larger than the available KV cache
memory (21.61 GiB). Based on the available memory, the estimated maximum model
length is 288.
```

On the same model and hardware, disabling hidden-state extraction allows a
maximum model length of 256,000. The failure is therefore specific to the
hidden-state cache being included in capacity accounting.

### Root cause

Hidden-state extraction registers a `CacheOnlyAttentionLayer` backed by
`HiddenStateCacheSpec`. Because `HiddenStateCacheSpec` inherits from
`MLAAttentionSpec`, DeepSeek-V4's model-specific grouping path classifies it as
a regular MLA layer.

For four bf16 hidden states with hidden size 4096 and block size 256, the
hidden-state page is approximately 8 MiB:

```text
256 * 4 * 4096 * 2 bytes = 8 MiB
```

This page is included in DeepSeek-V4 MLA packing and causes the compressor and
sliding-window cache pages to be padded to 8 MiB. The generic logic that
separates `HiddenStateCacheSpec` is not reached because the DeepSeek-V4 branch
returns earlier. The affected grouping and early-return logic remained
unchanged in the subsequent release inspected during this investigation, so
the bug persists wherever this original code path is present.

### Expected behavior

The hidden-state cache should be excluded from DeepSeek-V4 MLA/SWA tuple
grouping, restored exactly once as an independent cache group, and accounted
for using its own page geometry. Enabling hidden-state extraction should not
inflate the page sizes or memory estimates of the attention cache groups.

With the hidden-state cache isolated, the same startup reaches KV-cache
initialization and reports:

```text
Available KV cache memory: 21.61 GiB
GPU KV cache size: 6,199 tokens
Maximum concurrency for 8,192 tokens per request: 0.76x
```

The incorrect 581.48 GiB estimate is no longer produced, and the engine
continues past the KV-cache validation that previously raised the exception.

### Additional context

- A fix and regression tests are available in
  [#53074](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53074).
- [#39949](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39949) added generic
  hidden-state cache isolation for hybrid-attention models, but that logic is
  below DeepSeek-V4's model-specific early return.
- [#50894](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50894) addresses a separate
  tensor-parallel page-size alignment issue.
- [#49811](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49811) adds Model Runner V2
  support for `extract_hidden_states`; it does not change DeepSeek-V4 KV-cache
  grouping.

## Before submitting a new issue

- [x] Searched open and closed vLLM issues for the DeepSeek-V4-specific
  `HiddenStateCacheSpec` grouping failure and found no existing report.
- [x] Asked the chatbot on the vLLM documentation site; it identified this as a
  known issue and pointed to the open fix in #53074.
- [x] Added the exact image, runtime, hardware, and serving configuration used
  for the failing baseline and patched validation run.
- [x] Checked the report for tokens, credentials, private URLs, internal model
  paths, and confidential data.
